title: Centered-square MGF bound for nonnegative parameters
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $Z:\Omega\to\bbr$ be measurable, and let $\sigma^2>0$. Suppose that for every $s\in\bbr$, $e^{sZ}$ is $\mu$-integrable and $\mathbb{E}_\mu[e^{sZ}]\le e^{\sigma^2s^2/2}$. For every $t$ with $0\le t\le1/(4\sigma^2)$, the function $e^{t(Z^2-\sigma^2)}$ is integrable and its expectation is at most $e^{2\sigma^4t^2}$.
hypotheses_covered: $e^{sZ}$ is integrable and its moment-generating function is bounded by $e^{\sigma^2s^2/2}$ for every real $s$
replaced:
Let $Z$ be a measurable real random variable on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$
which is strictly sub-Gaussian with variance proxy $\sigma^2 > 0$ (for every real $s$,
$e^{sZ}$ is integrable and $\E_\mu[e^{sZ}] \le e^{\sigma^2 s^2/2}$).  Then for every
$t$ with $0 \le t \le 1/(4\sigma^2)$, the function $e^{t(Z^2 - \sigma^2)}$ is
$\mu$-integrable and
\[
  \E_\mu\!\left[e^{t(Z^2 - \sigma^2)}\right] \;\le\; e^{2\sigma^4 t^2}.
\]
